answer: I found two articles in effect today that still tell customers to use a retired form. "Broken or replaced odometer" says to mark 'not actual mileage' on form NW-ODO-1. That form was retired on February 1, 2026, and replaced by NW-ODO-2. "Selling a family member's car for them" says to have the owner sign NW-POA-1 in front of a notary. NW-POA-1 was also retired on February 1, 2026, and replaced by NW-POA-2, and even older signed copies were only accepted until June 30, 2026. Two other articles, "What to bring to your appraisal appointment" and "When more than one person owns the car", name the retired forms but only to say they were replaced, and they point customers to NW-ODO-2 and NW-POA-2, so they don't need fixing.
